summary: A Georgia list places a thomson tower in McDuffie County; a 2017 blog post under the heading Old Fire Watch Tower in Thomson includes an undated signed note saying a grandfather once worked in that tower; no source gives its history or the site today.

evidence.supports: Thomson entry: McDuffie County, coordinates, and 531 in the elevation column
Blog post is headed as an old fire watch tower in Thomson
evidence.quote: Old Fire Watch Tower in Thomson

evidence.supports: The blog post is dated 11 October 2017
A note says her grandfather used to work in the tower
evidence.quote: My grandfather used to work in this watch tower.

evidence.supports: The note is signed Tara Taylor
NHLR describes a McDuffie County lookout that appears to be an 82-foot Aermotor LS-40 with steel cab
evidence.quote: This lookout appears to be an 82-foot Aermotor LS-40 galvanized tower with a 7'x7'x10' steel cab.

evidence.supports: That NHLR lookout sits next to an active Georgia Forestry Commission office
evidence.quote: It is located next to an active Georgia Forestry Commission office.

evidence.supports: NHLR coordinates for that lookout, different from the list point
Statewide shift from staffed tower operators to air patrol in the late 1980s
evidence.quote: In the late 1980s, the Georgia Forestry Commission began phasing out the tower operators in favor of an air patrol system.

sources.title: Old Fire Watch Tower in Thomson

notes_for_editor: The NHLR McDuffie Lookout (US 1069, GA 18) is at 33.445348, -82.542365, roughly 12 km from the list point by my own calculation, so the story does not treat it as the list's thomson tower. A human should check whether the list point is mis-plotted, or whether the blog's Thomson tower is the NHLR one. The blog note is a personal recollection with no date. The list's elevation (531) has no unit; the record's 161.8 m assumes feet. The Wikipedia town centre (33.46722, -82.49944) is about 9 km south of the list point by my calculation.
